name: Vial of prophylactic antivenom
description: An experimental antivenom for injection. Taken some hours before a bite or sting, it blunts the venom. Needs a syringe.
notes: A liquid, so the item is the whole 10 ml vial and the row carries the reference's 40 g. plastic-amber draws the amber vial; it stays see-through in the game. The green flip-off cap sets it apart from the other vials. Venom protection and needing a syringe have no content fields yet.

name: Bottle of fluoxetine
description: An antidepressant. Lifts mood over days and changes how some other drugs act.
notes: The id names the drug instead of the reference's brand. Mood and drug interactions have no content fields yet.

name: Carton of Prussian blue capsules
description: An iron dye taken by mouth. Binds radioactive caesium and thallium in the gut so the body sheds them.
notes: The reference calls it a tablet; the medicine is sold as capsules. The radiation trefoil on the face marks it apart from the other cartons. Radiation has no content field yet.

name: Sachet of clotting powder
description: A sachet of granules poured into a wound. Turns blood to gel and stops heavy bleeding.
notes: The id describes the product instead of the reference's brand. Loose powder, so the model is the sealed single-use sachet a player picks up; one sachet is one item and carries the reference's 5 g. CHECK VOLUME is that sachet: flat and wide against a 5 ml dose. Bleeding treatment should follow the existing bandage's fields when the refactor applies drafts.

name: Saline bag
description: A bag of sterile salt water. Runs into a vein through a drip, or rinses grit and chemicals out of the eyes.
notes: A liquid, so the item is the whole 250 ml drip bag and the row carries 0.27 kg with it, against the reference's per-unit 51 g; the look step allows this as a per-unit reference. plastic-clear draws the bag; it stays see-through in the game. Fluid loss and eye rinsing have no content fields yet.

name: Spray bottle of skunk wash
description: A homemade mix of peroxide, baking soda and soap. Washes the stink of skunk spray out of skin and clothes.
notes: The id shortens the reference's. Crafted by the player, so usage is empty. A liquid, so the item is the whole 250 ml reused spray bottle and the row carries 0.28 kg with it, against the reference's per-unit 28 g; the look step allows this as a per-unit reference. The tape strip marks it as homemade. plastic-frosted draws the bottle. Smell has no content field yet.

name: Bottle of steroid eye drops
description: Corticosteroid drops. Calm red, swollen and irritated eyes.
notes: A liquid, so the item is the whole 5 ml dropper bottle and the row carries 4 g with it, against the reference's single drop of 3 g and 1 ml; CHECK VOLUME is that choice. The tall pink cap sets it apart from the plain eye drops. Eye inflammation has no content field yet.

name: Blister card of broad-spectrum antibiotics
description: Strong antibiotic capsules. One dose holds off any bacterial infection for twelve hours. Hard on the body.
notes: The id says what the reference's 'strong' means. The red and yellow capsules set it apart from the existing tetracycline. Its treatment should outrank tetracycline's when the refactor applies drafts; the dose duration has no content field yet.

name: Blister strip of chlorpromazine
description: An antipsychotic. Stops hallucinations and steadies the mind. Makes the taker drowsy.
notes: The id names the drug instead of the reference's brand. paint-terracotta stands in for the orange sugar coat. Round tablets come out blocky at 2 mm grain, the finest the lattice allows. Hallucination and sedation have no content fields yet.

name: Bottle of thyme oil
description: An essential oil pressed from thyme. A mild antiseptic that stings on a wound.
notes: A liquid, so the item is the whole 30 ml cobalt dropper bottle and the row carries 60 g with the glass, against the reference's 40 g; the reference's 250 ml is a carried volume, not this small bottle. plastic-clear-blue draws the cobalt glass; it stays see-through in the game. Crafted by the player as well as found, so Residential covers the found copies. Its antiseptic effect should sit below the existing antiseptic's.

name: Pouch of rolling tobacco
description: Loose fine-cut tobacco. Rolled into a cigarette with papers or smoked in a pipe. Addictive.
notes: The id says what kind of tobacco. Loose leaf, so the model is the folding pouch a player picks up. Smoking and nicotine have no content fields yet.

name: Vial of tramadol
description: A mild opioid painkiller. Eases moderate pain for several hours.
notes: The blue cap sets it apart from the other amber vials. plastic-amber stays see-through in the game. The analgesic numbers belong to the refactor; it should sit between aspirin and codeine and share the opioid cap.

name: Bottle of multivitamins
description: Daily tablets of vitamins and minerals. Fills gaps in a poor diet; too many cause illness.
notes: Gummy vitamins look the same in the bottle, so they ride on this model. The reference also lists an empty supplement bottle as a variant; it shares this model too, as the bottle with nothing in it. Nutrition has no content field yet.

name: Vitamin C fragment
description: A broken piece of a large vitamin C tablet.
notes: A piece a player breaks off a tablet, so the model is the piece itself: half of a large oval tablet, 20 mm by 9 mm, at the reference's 0.2 g. At 2 mm grain, the finest the lattice allows, the rounded edge comes out stepped. enamel-white stands in for the chalky tablet. Nutrition has no content field yet.

name: Tube of vitamin C tablets
description: Large vitamin C tablets. Keep scurvy away.
notes: The orange label and yellow cap stand for citrus. Nutrition has no content field yet.
